We have gone through her evidence to find that she has reported the incident to her parents on the date the incident has occurred.
Her evidence does not show that she and respondent had repetitive sexual intercourse.
What transpires from her evidence is that at the first instance when respondent forced himself on her, she lodged a complaint with her parents.
Such reaction, in our view, is indicative of the fact that she has not given consent.
Infact it is not even the case of the respondent, as nothing has been put up to the victim, that they were involved in consensual relations for some period.
That being so, even if it is presumed that she was capable of giving consent, the evidence indicate otherwise.
4. The appellant has thus made out a case for granting leave to file appeal.
Accordingly, the leave is granted.
Appeal be registered.
5. The observation made herein above, shall be understood and considered for the purpose of granting leave to file appeal.
